newsitem.title: UK: Branson's balloon adventure ends early, but safely.
newsitem.headline: Branson's balloon adventure ends early, but safely.

text.p: Richard Branson's attempt to be the first person to fly round the world by balloon ended on Wednesday less than 24 hours after it began, when technical problems forced him to land in the Algerian desert.
"The eagle has landed. No damage to capsule," the millionaire entrepreneur told his project team in London.
Project director Mike Kendrick told reporters that the balloon landed at 0729 GMT. "There were no injuries," he said.
Branson told his team in London that Alex Ritchie, a last-minute replacement as a co-pilot alongside Per Lindstrand, had probably saved their lives during the descent.
Ritchie climbed out of the capsule to release fuel cannisters, allowing the balloon to rise above a mountain range and land safely on a plain.

"We owe a debt of gratitude to Alex," Branson was quoted as saying. An Algerian helicopter was on its way to pick up the three men who landed near Bechar, 70 kms (45 miles) inside Algeria's border with Morocco.
Officials said the balloon's problems seemed to stem from the ratio of ballast to helium.
"The nature of the problem we are still trying to establish. I honestly can't tell you what it is, except that we know it's a ballast versus helium problem," Kendrick said.
Virgin officials cast doubt on whether Branson would have enough time for a second attempt this year. He failed to get off the ground last year because of unfavourable weather conditions.
The balloon -- reckoned to be the biggest in the world -- had set off under the media spotlight on Tuesday from an airfield near the Moroccan city of Marrakesh.

The officials had said they anticipated a calm landing. The lives of Branson and his two co-pilots were not in danger, they added. "There are no injuries involved, this is purely technical," Kendrick said.
Kendrick said Branson had contacted him by radio telephone from the balloon about the technical problem.
"Richard said, typically: 'I am sorry to disappoint you, Mike, we are having to land. We have got a duration problem. Please say sorry to everybody, and we will talk to you later'."

After taking off, the balloon had headed up into the jetstream they hoped would carry them across North Africa, Saudi Arabia, India, the South China Sea, the Pacific and the United States before landing in Britain after a 24,000-mile (38,600 km) trip expected to take between 14 and 21 days.
Branson had been racing against American balloonist Steve Fosset who is planning a similar round-the-world attempt, launched from St. Louis, Missouri.
Branson, flamboyant 46-year-old head of the Virgin group of companies, has launched an airline and products ranging from condoms to cola and pensions.
The tycoon has already crossed the Atlantic and Pacific by balloon.
